subject: Biology
title: Structural Organisation in Animals
summary: Animal tissues are of four types: epithelial (covering), connective (support and binding), muscular (movement) and neural (control).
Epithelia are simple or compound and may be squamous, cuboidal, columnar or ciliated; glands are epithelial cells specialised for secretion. Cell junctions (tight, adhering, gap) join cells.
Connective tissue includes loose and dense connective tissue, cartilage, bone, blood and adipose tissue. Muscles are skeletal, smooth or cardiac.
The frog (Rana tigrina) is studied as a model vertebrate: its morphology, digestive, respiratory, circulatory, excretory, nervous and reproductive systems.

formulas.name: Simple epithelium
formulas.formula: squamous — blood vessel walls, air sacs of lungs;  cuboidal — ducts of glands, PCT of nephron (brush border);  columnar — stomach and intestine lining (microvilli);  ciliated — bronchioles, fallopian tubes

formulas.name: Compound epithelium
formulas.formula: multi-layered; protective (skin, buccal cavity, pharynx, ducts of salivary and pancreatic glands)
formulas.when: Where protection from chemical and mechanical stress is needed.

formulas.name: Glands
formulas.formula: exocrine (with ducts — saliva, mucus, milk, earwax, digestive enzymes);  endocrine (ductless — hormones into blood)

formulas.name: Cell junctions
formulas.formula: tight junctions stop leakage;  adhering junctions cement cells together;  gap junctions connect cytoplasm for rapid transfer of ions and small molecules

formulas.name: Connective tissue types
formulas.formula: loose: areolar (under skin), adipose (fat);  dense regular: tendons (muscle → bone), ligaments (bone → bone);  dense irregular: skin;  specialised: cartilage, bone, blood
formulas.note: Blood is a fluid connective tissue.

formulas.name: Cartilage and bone
formulas.formula: cartilage: chondrocytes in lacunae, pliable matrix (nose tip, outer ear, between vertebrae);  bone: osteocytes in lacunae, hard matrix of calcium salts and collagen; bone marrow makes blood cells

formulas.name: Muscle types
formulas.formula: skeletal: striated, voluntary, multinucleate;  smooth: non-striated, involuntary, spindle-shaped (gut, blood vessels);  cardiac: striated, involuntary, branched, intercalated discs

formulas.name: Neural tissue
formulas.formula: neurons (excitable) + neuroglia (support and protect; more than half the volume of neural tissue)

formulas.name: Frog heart and blood
formulas.formula: 3 chambers (2 atria + 1 ventricle) inside a pericardium;  sinus venosus joins the right atrium and receives blood from the body through the venae cavae;  conus arteriosus on the ventral side;  closed circulation + lymphatic system;  RBCs nucleated;  hepatic portal system = liver ↔ intestine;  renal portal system = kidney ↔ lower parts of the body

formulas.name: Frog respiration
formulas.formula: in water: skin ONLY (cutaneous — dissolved O₂ diffuses through the moist skin);  on land: skin + buccal cavity + lungs (pulmonary);  during hibernation/aestivation: skin
formulas.note: Trap: the skin keeps working on land too. 'Skin + buccal cavity in water' is false; 'skin + buccal cavity + lungs on land' is true.

formulas.name: Frog excretion
formulas.formula: ureotelic;  kidneys → ureters → cloaca;  in males the ureter is a urinogenital duct; in females ureters and oviducts open separately into the cloaca

formulas.name: Frog nervous system
formulas.formula: 10 pairs of cranial nerves;  brain = forebrain (olfactory lobes, cerebral hemispheres, diencephalon), midbrain (optic lobes), hindbrain (cerebellum, medulla oblongata)

formulas.name: Frog reproduction
formulas.formula: external fertilisation in water;  development via tadpole larva (metamorphosis);  female lays 2500–3000 ova at a time

examples.title: Tendon vs ligament
examples.problem: What does a tendon connect, and what does a ligament connect?
examples.solution: Tendon: skeletal muscle to bone. Ligament: bone to bone. Both are dense regular connective tissue.

examples.title: Which muscle?
examples.problem: A muscle is striated, branched and involuntary, with intercalated discs. Which type?
examples.solution: Cardiac muscle — the intercalated discs (fused plasma membranes with gap junctions) let the cells contract as a unit.

examples.title: Brush border
examples.problem: Where is cuboidal epithelium with a brush border found?
examples.solution: In the proximal convoluted tubule (PCT) of the nephron; microvilli increase the surface for reabsorption.

examples.title: Frog skin
examples.problem: Why is frog skin always moist?
examples.solution: Mucous glands keep it moist. A moist skin is needed for cutaneous respiration — the only route of gas exchange in water and during hibernation/aestivation, and still used on land along with the buccal cavity and lungs.

examples.title: Male or female frog?
examples.problem: How do you tell a male frog from a female?
examples.solution: Males have vocal sacs and a copulatory pad on the first digit of each forelimb; females lack both.

examples.title: Areolar tissue
examples.problem: What cells does areolar tissue contain?
examples.solution: Fibroblasts (make fibres), macrophages and mast cells, in a semi-fluid ground substance with collagen and elastic fibres.

topics.title: Organ and organ system
topics.explain: Tissues form organs (stomach, lung, heart, kidney); organs form organ systems (digestive, respiratory). Complexity in organ and organ systems displays a recognisable trend through evolution.

topics.title: Blood
topics.explain: A fluid connective tissue: plasma + formed elements (RBCs, WBCs, platelets). It is the main circulating fluid that transports substances.

topics.title: Frog morphology
topics.explain: Body divisible into head and trunk; no neck or tail. Skin smooth and slippery; dorsal side olive green with dark spots, ventral side pale yellow. Frogs don't drink water but absorb it through the skin. They show camouflage (mimicry) and are cold-blooded (poikilothermous).

topics.title: Frog digestive system
topics.explain: Short alimentary canal (frogs are carnivores). Bilobed tongue catches insects. Liver secretes bile (stored in gall bladder); pancreas secretes pancreatic juice. Digestion completes in the intestine; food is absorbed by villi and microvilli. Undigested waste leaves through the cloaca.

topics.title: Frog sense organs
topics.explain: Sense organs: touch (sensory papillae), taste (taste buds), smell (nasal epithelium), vision (eyes) and hearing (tympanum with internal ear). Eyes and internal ears are well organised; the rest are cellular aggregations around nerve endings.

topics.title: Endocrine glands in frog
topics.explain: Pituitary, thyroid, parathyroid, thymus, pineal body, pancreatic islets, adrenals and gonads.

ratta: Squamous — air sacs;  cuboidal — PCT;  columnar — gut;  ciliated — bronchioles, fallopian tube.
Tight stops leakage;  adhering cements;  gap connects cytoplasm.
Frog: 3-chambered heart, nucleated RBCs, 10 cranial nerves, ureotelic.
Male frog: vocal sacs + copulatory pad.
Frog breathing: water = skin only;  land = skin + buccal cavity + lungs;  hibernation/aestivation = skin.
Frog portals: hepatic = liver–intestine;  renal = kidney–lower body;  venae cavae → sinus venosus → right atrium.
